title: Smoke without fire: a different view of the cigar galaxy
caption: The core of the Cigar Galaxy, Messier 82, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Cigar Galaxy, M 82, M82, Messier 82 · constellation Ursa Major · about 12 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Glowing gas and dark dust lanes dominate this view of the core of Messier 82, the Cigar Galaxy, while its stars appear faint. It was the most detailed image ever made of this starburst galaxy, which lies about 12 million light-years away in Ursa Major, the Great Bear.

Earlier Hubble pictures showed Messier 82 blazing with stars. The difference comes from the filters. Hubble's cameras record only in grayscale, and color images are built by combining exposures taken through different filters.

Broad filters, close to the colors our eyes see, give natural-looking images with bright stars. The filters used here instead pass only the light given off by particular chemical elements. That isolates the glowing gas clouds and blocks much of the starlight, so the stars fade and the dust lanes stand out sharply against the bright gas.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.71 x 2.66 arcminutes) and distance (12 million light years), the frame spans roughly 9,500 × 9,300 light-years. Its light set out about 12 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3, using narrow filters for specific elements. Sulfur is shown in red, visible light from oxygen in green, ultraviolet light from oxygen in blue, and hydrogen in cyan.
understand.eye: The eye sees starlight across all colors at once, so it could never isolate the glow of individual elements the way these filters do, and part of the data is ultraviolet.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Messier 82 is rich in dust, young stars and glowing gas, and it is both unusually bright and fairly close to Earth. The field of view is about 2.7 by 2.7 arcminutes.
alt: The core of a galaxy dominated by glowing gas clouds with sharp dark dust lanes and faint stars.
